punchline: On Everest in 1996 the turnaround time was two o'clock, and a client was still reaching the summit after four.
thirty_sec: On 10 May 1996 guides on Everest had set a two o'clock turnaround time. Many climbers were still going up after that, and Rob Hall stayed with his client Doug Hansen, who reached the summit after four. A storm came that evening, and eight people died over two days. Jon Krakauer, who was there, ties it to decisions on the mountain, including a rule that stayed on paper.
